findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics when the file does not exist or is unreadable
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadMetricsError> and use .map_err(|e| LoadMetricsError::Io(e))

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) performs I/O inside what should be a parsing step
findings.failure_mode: pure data parsing is fused with shell-side logging; side effects leak into the calculation layer, making the function non-deterministic and untestable
findings.fix: remove println! from load_metrics; logging belongs exclusively in the action/shell layer that calls this function

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked slice indexing without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: a malformed line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields causes a panic at runtime instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use parts.get(0).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) and parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) with map_err

findings.failure_mode: invalid numeric field in a CSV line aborts the program instead of returning a typed ParseError::Invalid
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) and propagate via Result

findings.problem: as u16 performs a lossy truncating cast from u32 to u16 with no range check
findings.failure_mode: values in range 65536..=4294967295 silently wrap to 0..=2791631763, producing incorrect domain values without any error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) for a checked conversion

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates a Vec<String> for every line
findings.failure_mode: unbounded intermediate allocation per line; violates allocation discipline and Functional Core principle; also parses all fields when only first two are needed
findings.fix: use let (name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; parse value_str.trim() directly

findings.problem: load_metrics fuses file I/O (Action), parsing (Calculation), and domain construction (Data) in a single function
findings.failure_mode: violates Data/Calculations/Actions architecture; shell side-effects leak into data loading; impossible to test parsing logic in isolation
findings.fix: split into: (1) parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> for pure calculation, (2) load_metrics(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadMetricsError> for shell I/O orchestration

findings.problem: pub value: u16 exposes a raw primitive in the domain struct without a newtype wrapper
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct Record with any u16 value, including invalid domain states; no invariant enforcement on the value field
findings.fix: create a MetricValue newtype struct with a private constructor that validates the range, and use it in Record

findings.problem: raw String primitives from split cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; callers can construct invalid domain states from unvalidated input
findings.failure_mode: the parse boundary does not enforce invariants; invalid data shapes produce panics or silent truncation rather than typed errors at the parse point
findings.fix: define ParseError enum with Invalid/Overflow variants; use split_once with ok_or for shape validation; use try_from for width conversion; use smart constructor on Record

findings.problem: no try_reserve or domain cap on the Vec allocation; file size directly controls allocation magnitude
findings.failure_mode: an attacker or misconfigured system can supply an arbitrarily large file, causing unbounded heap allocation and potential OOM crash
findings.fix: add a max_records parameter or constant cap; call values.try_reserve(min(cap, file_line_count)).map_err(|_| LoadMetricsError::Allocation) before the iterator

findings.problem: parse::<u32>() followed by as u16 uses unchecked arithmetic path: no checked_add, checked_div, or checked_cast anywhere
findings.failure_mode: arithmetic side effects are unguarded; overflow and truncation produce silent data corruption rather than typed errors
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) for a checked width conversion returning typed error

no profiler data identifying hot paths in parsing
no allocation budget or try_reserve evidence for Vec capacity
no second-ring evidence (benchmark, profiler, or measured data) for any performance claim

residual_risk: This crate has pervasive violations of Holzman absolute laws: five unwrap surfaces, unchecked indexing, lossy casts, hidden I/O in parsing logic, fused shell/core responsibilities, raw primitive domain state, and unbounded allocation. No verified evidence exists. Delivery is blocked until all findings are remediated with Result-returning APIs, typed error taxonomy, split_once parsing, checked conversions, and architecture separation.
